task: Derive on_fail state read/write metadata from the handler's declared domain state.
observation: The Java Margo interface writer decided whether a failure arm accessed state by searching for the fixture field name `count` in statement text, then emitted hardcoded `count` read/write records. It now visits actual declared state fields and detects assignment writes and expression reads for each failure arm. State consumption and local capture serialization are still not inferred by this writer.
impact: A failure arm using a differently named state field now emits matching read/write metadata in the focused producer test. This is a direct-statement projection only and does not establish complete source-free exception metadata or native compatibility.

resolution.summary: Focused ABI-v10 producer coverage derives a `retries` state read and write; all ten Java test classes pass in staged ABI-v10 and default ABI-v9 runs. State consumes and source-free native validation remain open.

task: Emit source-free failure capture rows from checker-proved captures and types.
observation: The Java Margo interface writer used handler names `Run`/`Join` and local spellings `attempt`/`joined` to select captures, then emitted a four-field row that did not match the ABI-v9 capture record. The checker now retains type facts for locals proven initialized and unmoved on matching direct raise edges, and the producer emits counted captures plus recursively fingerprinted owned type shapes from those facts.
impact: A focused project-interface producer case now checks the canonical ABI-v9 failure capture row and scalar type-shape record for an `Int` capture, independent of handler/local names. Capture facts remain limited to explicit raises; source-free Java loading of failure-arm records, call-propagated captures, and native provider-consumer behavior remain unverified.

resolution.summary: The focused producer assertion passes for a checker-proven scalar capture with canonical fields and fingerprint. Full Java suites pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10; native ABI parsing/linkage and non-scalar capture shapes remain unverified.

task: Restore source-free ABI-v9 failure-arm and capture facts in the Java compiler AST.
observation: The Java .mossi loader ignored handler_failure_arm and handler_failure_capture records, so imported domains lost exported on_fail pattern and capture type facts despite the producer emitting them.
impact: A focused loader regression now observes the imported Fault.Bad arm and Int capture on a source-free domain. This establishes Java AST restoration only; cross-crate native propagation and capture lifetime behavior remain unverified.

resolution.summary: The focused source-free metadata test passes for ABI-v9 and ABI-v10 exercised paths. Native provider-consumer behavior remains open.

task: Mirror and validate canonical ABI-v10 open callable summary records in Java.
observation: The Java ABI-v10 record adapter implemented nominal and method templates but had no open-summary codec; the source-free verifier therefore could not validate typed public summary record bytes or their record identities.
impact: Java now encodes/decodes canonical summary v3/v4 structures and verifies typed public summaries. A fixed C++ generated payload and ID match byte-for-byte, and a forged-ID record is rejected. ProjectBuilder summary derivation, checked-body records, and source-free checker projection remain unimplemented.

resolution.summary: All ten Java unit-test classes pass in default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10 modes. C++-generated v3 payload/ID and v4 Callable-effect ID match; a v2 legacy payload paired with the C++ canonical re-encoded ID is accepted by both C++ validate_summary and the Java decoder. End-to-end Java ABI-v10 callable production/import remains open.

task: Mirror and verify canonical ABI-v10 checked-body record envelopes in Java.
observation: Java could encode textual checked-body fixtures but had no codec for the canonical private checked-body record envelope, and its source-free verifier did not bind a binary checked body to the callable summary hash or callable body dependencies.
impact: Java now round-trips and validates canonical checked-body records and IR, and the production verifier enforces summary/body hash and callable dependency links plus summary/requirement provenance references. A fixed record payload matches C++ checked_body_record. Producer derivation from checked functions, loader projection, and nominal-dependency closure remain open.

resolution.summary: All ten Java unit-test classes pass after clean builds in default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10 modes; canonical checked-body bytes match C++ and verifier tests cover missing/mismatched summaries. End-to-end Java callable source-free production/import and nominal dependency closure remain open.

task: Validate ABI-v10 checked-body nominal-template dependency hashes during source-free admission.
observation: The Java source-free verifier decoded checked-body dependency envelopes but only validated callable dependencies; a body could name a nominal template with an unrelated representation hash and still pass this closure check.
impact: The verifier now checks dependencies that resolve to ABI-v10 nominal templates against their representation hash. Focused coverage accepts a correct hash and rejects a forged hash. Private enum dependency projection remains outside this fix, so unknown nominal dependency kinds are not resolved here.

resolution.summary: The template representation-hash check passes all ten Java test classes under default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Private enum dependency decoding and full checked-body closure remain open.

task: Decode canonical ABI-v10 private enum declarations and validate checked-body links to them.
observation: Java source-free verification had no private enum record decoder, so it could not distinguish a valid enum body dependency from a missing or forged declaration hash. A fixed private enum payload and dependency hash were compared against the C++ ABI implementation.
impact: A Java codec now validates private enum identities, variant and payload field shape, canonical bytes, module/provenance links, and dependency hashes. The focused test admits a valid link and rejects a forged link. This codec/verification slice does not mean ProjectBuilder produces private enum records or that the loader projects them into semantic checking.

resolution.summary: All ten Java unit-test classes pass in default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10 modes. Producer derivation and source-free checker projection remain open. Fixed C++-generated payload bytes and enum dependency hash match the Java codec.

task: Project checker inference variables into callable summary bound ordinals.
observation: The Java ABI-v10 TypeRef projection only handled closed types, so checker-retained open TypeVars could not be turned into summary BoundVar wire types.
impact: An overload now accepts the callable TypeVarId-to-ordinal map, preserves repeated references through nested builtin types, and rejects an open variable without an assigned summary ordinal. This is a conversion primitive; ProjectBuilder summary/body production and consumer projection remain open.

resolution.summary: All ten Java unit-test classes pass in default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Tests cover Vector[TypeVar] mapping to Vector[_0] and fail-closed missing ordinal handling.

task: Project bounded source-free ABI-v10 direct-return, literal, integer-arithmetic, and collection bodies.
observation: The Java source-free loader verified ABI-v10 typed summary and checked-body records but discarded them before semantic checking, leaving imported callable behavior dependent on legacy generic text rows.
impact: The producer and loader now handle checked direct-parameter-return bodies across multiple parameters, zero-argument signed integer/float, boolean, and plain String constants, one-parameter closed-Int binary arithmetic with nonnegative integer literals, and nested built-in signatures such as Vector[Int]. A producer-to-loader regression strips legacy generic body rows, then checks each shape and the generic Int/String specializations. General callable bodies, String escape decoding, nominal wire type resolution, generic operator requirements/effects, and native provider-consumer behavior remain open.

resolution.summary: All ten Java unit-test classes pass in default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10 modes; source-free typed direct-return, numeric/boolean/plain-String constants, all five closed-Int arithmetic operators, and Vector[Int] consumer checks pass. General ABI-v10 callable projection and native compatibility remain unverified.

task: Expand source-free ABI-v10 checked-body projection for checked, closed-Int expression returns.
observation: The Java ABI-v10 producer and loader admitted only a single Int parameter combined with one nonnegative literal, even though the checked-body codec already represents nested arithmetic and unary operations. A source-free exported function using two Int parameters, nested arithmetic, or unary negation therefore had no typed body record.
impact: The producer now lowers bounded closed-Int return expressions containing Int parameters, integer literals, parentheses, unary negation, and nested +, -, *, /, and % operations. The loader reconstructs Moss expressions from checked IR with parameter ordinals resolved against the imported signature. Positive coverage checks a two-parameter mixed-precedence body and unary negation after legacy generic rows are removed. Other result types, statements, calls, and effects remain outside this slice.

resolution.summary: All ten Java unit-test classes pass after clean builds in default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10 modes. Agent feedback validation and git diff checks pass. Native execution, Rust compilation, Margo provider-consumer integration, SDK compatibility, and full acceptance remain unverified.

task: Verify and correct Java checked-body-v1 framing against the C++ ABI-v10 implementation.
observation: Java checked-body round trips were self-consistent but encoded statement framing differently from C++ and counted Java characters rather than UTF-8 bytes in field lengths. Its default expression branch also serialized unsupported node kinds as literal payloads, masking the incompatibility.
impact: Java now uses the C++ checked-body-v1 root-return and statement layouts for its supported expression and statement nodes, sorts nominal field substitutions canonically, frames fields by UTF-8 byte length, and rejects unsupported checked-body node kinds. Java reproduces the C++ fixture hash for `return x * 2 + 20`; a non-ASCII String body round-trips with byte-correct framing. This does not implement all C++ checked-body expression/statement variants.

resolution.summary: All ten Java unit-test classes pass in default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10 after clean builds. The Java checked body matches the C++ canonical arithmetic hash and UTF-8 framing regression passes. Unsupported IR kinds still fail closed; complete C++ node coverage and native provider-consumer integration remain open.

task: Retain structured payloads for additional canonical checked-body expression and statement nodes.
observation: Java checked-body node objects lacked fields needed to round-trip message targets, pipeline metadata, constructor payload identities, match arms, and exception branches. The encoder/reader previously supported only a subset of the canonical wire variants.
impact: The checked-body Java model and codec now retain and encode/decode message, member-call, pipeline map/placeholder, nominal/enum construction, Match, Try, and Raise payloads. A focused multi-node round-trip exercises representative extended forms. This improves wire representation only; full semantic validation, loader projection, generated Rust correctness, and native source-free compatibility remain unproven.

resolution.summary: All ten Java unit-test classes pass in default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10 modes. The checked-body round-trip covers representative message, member-call, pipeline-map, nominal/enum construction, Match, Try, and Raise nodes. Full ABI semantic parity and native consumer compatibility remain open.

task: Project bounded pure Float arithmetic through canonical ABI-v10 source-free callable records.
observation: ABI-v10 typed callable production and source-free loading covered direct Float literals but omitted checked arithmetic over Float parameters, despite the codec representing Float expressions.
impact: The producer now emits canonical summary and checked-body records for single-return Float expressions over Float parameters using +, -, *, /, parentheses, unary negation, and Moss NumericLiteral canonicalization. The source-free loader projects only matching typed Float trees. An end-to-end Java metadata test removes legacy generic body rows before loading and checking two calls. This does not prove native Rust compilation/execution or general ABI-v10 body support.

resolution.summary: All ten Java unit-test classes pass in default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10; both C++ and Java accept the focused Float source probe. Producer/loader metadata tests check Float addition, division, multiplication, unary negation, .5 and underscore canonicalization with legacy body rows removed. Native compilation, execution, and Margo integration remain unverified.

task: Project bounded Int comparison predicates as source-free ABI-v10 callables.
observation: The ABI-v10 source-free projection path admitted Int expression returns and Bool constants but could not carry a checked Int comparison returning Bool.
impact: The producer now records Bool-returning checked bodies for one top-level Int comparison with Int-typed operands, including arithmetic operands. The loader reconstructs only recognized comparison tags whose child trees match the Int parameter summary. The producer-consumer unit test removes legacy generic body text and checks an imported predicate call. Other Bool expressions and general callable bodies remain open.

resolution.summary: All ten Java unit-test classes pass in default and staged ABI-v10 modes. The typed producer and source-free consumer test covers Int > 0 returning Bool with legacy generic body rows removed; C++ and Java both accept the focused standalone probe. Native compatibility and broader Bool expressions remain unverified.

task: Carry logical combinations and negation of checked Int predicates through source-free ABI-v10.
observation: The source-free ABI-v10 predicate projection admitted only one Int comparison, preventing even checked combinations of comparisons from crossing a source-free module boundary.
impact: The bounded producer now encodes Bool literals, negation, and/or/xor trees over Int comparisons; the loader reconstructs only supported Boolean operators and typed Int comparison children. A source-free consumer test strips legacy body rows and checks chained comparisons plus negation. This remains a pure predicate subset and does not establish native execution or general callable body parity.

resolution.summary: All ten Java unit-test classes pass in default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Producer/consumer checks cover comparison conjunction and negation with legacy generic rows removed; both C++ and Java accept the standalone source probe. Native/backend compatibility and other Boolean forms remain open.

task: Extend checked ABI-v10 predicate projection to homogeneous Float comparisons.
observation: Source-free Boolean predicate records could carry comparisons over Int expressions but omitted the same comparison and logical forms over Float parameters.
impact: The ABI-v10 producer/loader now handles pure Bool predicates over homogeneous Int or Float parameters, including supported comparisons, logical composition, negation, and matching same-type arithmetic operands. The Java metadata test strips legacy body rows and checks a Float range predicate through a source-free consumer. Mixed numeric types and other Bool expressions remain unsupported.

resolution.summary: All ten Java unit-test classes pass in default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Producer/consumer tests exercise Float comparison composition with legacy body rows removed; C++ and Java accept the focused Float predicate probe. Native and broader ABI-v10 body behavior remain unverified.

task: Carry straight-line pure Int local declarations, assignments, and returns through ABI-v10 source-free callables.
observation: The Java ABI-v10 producer and loader only projected single-return bodies, despite the checked-body model and codec having typed Let, Var, Assign, LocalRead, and Return variants.
impact: The producer now lowers a bounded straight-line body of Int parameters, let/implicit mutable locals, reassignment, pass, and one final return into canonical checked IR. The source-free loader validates dense local ordinals, mutability, types, and prior local reads before reconstructing function statements. Producer-consumer checks remove legacy generic body text and cover immutable and mutable locals. Control flow, calls, effects, other types, and native behavior remain open.

resolution.summary: All ten Java unit-test classes pass in default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. The source-free producer/consumer test covers let, implicit mutable binding, reassignment, and return after legacy body rows are removed; C++ and Java both accept the standalone probe. Native/source-free execution and general statement-body parity remain unverified.

task: Generalize source-free ABI-v10 straight-line local-body projection from Int to Float.
observation: The first Float local consumer regression exposed two gaps: the producer/local reader path was Int-only, and parameter ordinal placeholders were not rebound inside reconstructed local statements, causing a mutable Float local to be inferred as Int.
impact: The producer now emits straight-line numeric local bodies for homogeneous Int or Float parameters/results. The loader validates numeric types, dense ordinals, mutability, and prior reads, then binds each parameter ordinal to the imported function’s own parameter name before semantic checking. Producer-consumer tests cover immutable and mutable Float locals. Control flow, calls, effects, other local types, and native compatibility remain open.

resolution.summary: The initial staged-ABI unit run caught the unresolved Float-local parameter placeholder. After rebinding the placeholder per imported callable, a clean build and all ten Java unit-test classes pass in both ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10 modes. The source-free producer/consumer test covers Float let, implicit mutable binding, reassignment, and return with legacy body text removed. C++ and Java accept the focused source probe.

task: Carry direct Int if/else return bodies across source-free ABI-v10 callables.
observation: The source-free ABI-v10 producer and loader projected direct returns and straight-line numeric locals but discarded an exported Int function with a simple conditional return in both branches.
impact: The producer now records one bounded checked If with one Int Return per arm, and the source-free loader reconstructs the Moss branch statements after validating expression types and rebinding parameter ordinals. The regression removes legacy generic body rows and runs semantic checking on the consumer. Nested or general control flow remains unsupported.

resolution.summary: Clean Java build and all ten Java unit-test classes pass in default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Native compilation/execution, Margo source-free integration, SDK compatibility, and broader control-flow projection remain unverified.

task: Generalize source-free ABI-v10 direct branch-return projection from Int to Float.
observation: The bounded ABI-v10 If projection handled Int branch values but omitted the same checked control-flow form for Float callables.
impact: The producer now lowers homogeneous Int or Float branch-return bodies, and the source-free loader reconstructs the matching numeric branch expressions from typed checked IR. The legacy generic body rows are removed in the producer-consumer regression before semantic checking. Nested control flow and other value types remain unsupported by this path.

resolution.summary: Clean build and all ten Java unit-test classes pass in default and staged ABI-v10 modes; C++ and Java both accept the focused Int/Float branch probe. Native compatibility, Margo integration, SDK gates, and general control flow remain unverified.

task: Project direct branch-return bodies with Bool results and numeric predicates through ABI-v10.
observation: The source-free ABI-v10 branch-return path handled numeric results but not a Bool-valued branch selected by a checked numeric predicate; the summary helper also assumed parameter types equal the result type.
impact: The producer now forms summaries from each checked parameter TypeRef and the checked result TypeRef, and lowers Bool branch values through supported checked predicate trees. The loader applies matching typed projection. Producer-consumer coverage strips legacy body text and semantically checks Int, Float, and Bool cases. General control flow and arbitrary Bool expressions remain unsupported.

resolution.summary: Clean build and all ten Java unit-test classes pass in default and staged ABI-v10 modes; C++ and Java both accept the focused Int/Float/Bool branch probe. Native compatibility, Margo integration, SDK gates, and general control flow remain unverified.

task: Replace fixture-name source-free diagnostics with checked-body availability facts.
observation: The source-free CLI rejected Provider.outer by hardcoded name and emitted a special Provider.relay error. Removing those guards exposed that the Java ABI writer serialized an inferred open Vector result as unit, producing a false return mismatch.
impact: The CLI now rejects an imported ABI-v10 call when its checked body was not projected, using a generic SOURCE_FREE_CHECKED_BODY_UNAVAILABLE diagnostic; the Provider.outer fixture guard is gone. The ABI writer preserves inferred open built-in result kinds. Generated-provider CLI regressions prove valid Provider.outer is accepted and unsupported Provider.relay fails closed, and inspect the inferred vector metadata. General source-free helper closure and execution remain open.

resolution.summary: Generated source-free CLI regression accepts valid Provider.outer and rejects unsupported Provider.relay with SOURCE_FREE_CHECKED_BODY_UNAVAILABLE. All ten Java unit-test classes pass in default and staged ABI-v10 modes. Native/Margo/SDK integration remains unverified.

task: Carry the checked empty-vector return body for an open generic result through source-free ABI-v10 imports.
observation: The ABI-v9 semantic record retained the inferred vector result kind after the previous fix, but ABI-v10 had no supported body profile for a zero-argument `return []` export. A source-free consumer therefore could not specialize the result type despite the checked-body codec supporting VectorLiteral.
impact: The producer now emits a typed one-variable summary and canonical VectorLiteral checked body for the narrow zero-argument empty-vector return form. The loader projects that exact form to a generic source-free function; regression checks specialize it as Vector[Int] and Vector[Bool]. Other collection expressions, helper calls, and native/source-free execution remain unverified.

resolution.summary: A producer-consumer semantic regression strips legacy generic body rows, validates the checked empty-vector summary/body, and specializes the import at Int and Bool element types. Clean Java build and all ten Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Native and Margo integration remain unverified.

task: Support source-free calls to explicit closed Vector[T] functions returning an empty vector.
observation: The newly added ABI-v10 empty-vector profile handled an inferred Vector[T] result, but the same checked VectorLiteral with a concrete Vector[Int] result was omitted by the producer and loader profile constraints.
impact: The empty-vector body profile now also emits and projects summaries with zero bound variables when the result is a closed vector type. Source-free consumer coverage semantically checks the concrete Vector[Int] import while retaining inferred Int and Bool specialization checks. Native execution and general collection code paths remain unverified.

resolution.summary: Clean build and all ten Java unit-test classes pass in staged ABI-v10 and default ABI-v9. The producer-consumer regression strips legacy generic body text and type-checks the source-free concrete Vector[Int] call plus inferred Int and Bool calls. Native and Margo integration remain unverified.

task: Serialize and source-free project nested primitive Vector return literals under ABI-v10.
observation: The Java ABI-v10 producer/loader handled closed primitive vectors but rejected nested vectors even though the checked-body schema can represent recursive VectorLiteral nodes.
impact: Producer lowering and source-free projection now recurse through closed Vector types with bounded depth and child-type checks. The provider-consumer regression strips legacy body rows, imports Vector[Vector[Int]], and executes an indexed read that returns 3. Both Java ABI unit suites pass all eleven classes.

resolution.summary: Closed nested primitive vector literals now produce checked ABI-v10 bodies and source-free consumer execution.

task: Retain empty inner vectors in recursive ABI-v10 checked-body literals.
observation: The first nested-vector profile failed closed when an inner literal was empty because top-level splitting represented the empty contents as a blank element.
impact: The recursive producer now treats an empty vector body as zero operands while preserving its checked nested Vector type. The provider regression verifies the empty VectorLiteral child, strips legacy body rows, and executes an indexed read from the source-free imported matrix. Both ABI unit suites pass all eleven classes.

resolution.summary: Empty nested VectorLiteral nodes are now emitted, imported, and retained in source-free execution.

task: Preserve valid Moss String escapes in ABI-v10 source-free vector literals.
observation: The closed ABI-v10 vector profile rejected all backslash characters in StringLiteral payloads, excluding valid escaped newlines and quotes from source-free Vector[String] returns.
impact: The producer and importer now validate escapes with Moss parser escape rules while retaining raw quote and line-break rejection. A source-free provider-consumer regression strips legacy rows and verifies escaped strings at runtime. Both ABI unit suites pass all eleven classes.

resolution.summary: Valid Moss escape sequences now round-trip through checked StringLiteral vector children and source-free consumer execution.

task: Import closed source-free ABI-v10 callables when the legacy v9 declaration row is absent.
observation: The Java source-free loader projected ABI-v10 checked bodies only onto functions first declared in the legacy semantic contract. A valid ABI-v10 summary/body pair therefore could not stand alone if the redundant legacy declaration was absent.
impact: The loader seeds closed callables from checked v10 summaries after legacy declarations are parsed. Its bounded generic profiles are direct parameter pass-through with one distinct BoundVar per parameter and a zero-parameter empty Vector[T] result; all require no requirements, dependencies, or effects. Both legacy copies are stripped in tests. Closed Int/Bool/Float/String and collection results, nested Vector[Vector[Int]], escaped Vector[String], (T)->T, (T,U)->U, and empty Vector[Int]/Vector[Bool] execute. Summary parameter access modes are preserved. Other generic relations, nominal methods, and effect/dependency-bearing callables remain outside this slice.

resolution.summary: ABI-v10-only imports pass for closed scalar and collection callables including Float/String literals, nested vectors and escaped String elements, direct generic parameter pass-through (T -> T and (T, U) -> U), and inferred empty Vector[T] specialized as Int and Bool; all eleven Java test classes pass in staged ABI-v10 and default ABI-v9.

task: Assess bounded generic ABI-v10-only declaration seeding without shared inference state.
observation: Binding summary BoundVar values directly as shared TypeRef.InferenceVar instances contaminated sequential calls. The retained seeding path instead leaves synthetic generic parameters unannotated and reconstructs only checked direct parameter-return bodies.
impact: ABI-v10-only source-free generic calls pass for T -> T and (T, U) -> U with Int and String arguments after both legacy declaration copies are removed. The zero-parameter empty Vector[T] profile also specializes as Int and Bool. Summary access modes are retained. Generic relations that combine or transform parameters remain unsupported.

resolution.summary: The direct generic pass-through and inferred empty-vector profiles execute independent Int/String/Bool calls and pass all eleven Java unit classes in staged ABI-v10 and default ABI-v9.
